newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta Freeport handles 15 pct more containers.
newsitem.headline: Malta Freeport handles 15 pct more containers.

text.p: Malta Freeport handled 514,767 containers on transhipment (TEUs) in 1996, an increase of 15 percent over 1995, the company reported on Wednesday.

Malta Freeport, which faces competition from the recently opened Gioia Tauro freeport in southern Italy, said 1996 was a crucial year during which it strengthened its position as the leading central Mediterranean transhipment hub.
During 1996 a consortium formed of Nippon Yusen Kaisha of Japan, Neptune Orient Lines of Singapore and Hapag-Lloyd of Germany, started operations to and from the port, the company said.
It said Mediterranean Shipping Company of Switzerland and Hyundai Merchant Marine of South Korea also started operations from Malta Freeport, which however lost Maersk Lines and Sea Land Service Inc.

Freeport chairman Marin Hili said the first phase of a new transhipment terminal at Marsaxlokk, on the southern tip of Malta, was due to be operational next July, increasing the annual handling capacity by 250,000 TEUs.
The freeport hopes to handle one million containers by the end of the century.
